name: cold_survey_line_v1
hypothesis: For installers whose own site says they visit to survey or measure (~140 after the no-pressure segment), naming that cost ('a trip out to measure up and an evening pricing it') gets more positive replies than the neutral cost line, because it makes the wasted effort concrete and personal.
variable: the cost sentence only (opener, offer line and ask identical to cold_offer_v1 arm A)
decision_rule: Directional only (~70 per arm). Keep the specific line if it has >= 80% probability of the higher positive-reply rate and no more opt-outs; then use 'name the real cost from their own site' as a pattern.

arms.subject: last year's quotes
arms.body:
Hi,

Ever had a homeowner ring back months after a quote, ready to go?

The ones who don't ring back are still sitting in {company}'s inbox. Each one cost you a lead, a trip out to measure and an evening pricing it.

I chase them in your name and put anyone still keen in your diary. You only pay for surveys that get booked.

Worth a look?
